economy.summary: Her platform calls for raising the minimum wage to a viable level, guaranteed paid family leave, and keeping the cost of food down, and proposes job creation through streamlined business licensing, mentorships and grants for new businesses, and support for ecological and historical tourism.
economy.short: Supports raising minimum wage, paid family leave, small-business grants.

taxes.summary: In a VOTE411 questionnaire, said the state budget should be helped by streamlining business licensing and by exploring new revenue sources such as legalizing marijuana and taxing skill games.
taxes.short: Proposes revenue from marijuana legalization and taxing skill games.

education.summary: Supports increasing subsidies for daycare and creating universal pre-K, expanding free job training and dual enrollment programs, and capping tuition at Pennsylvania higher-education institutions; her site also calls for increasing funding for public schools.
education.short: Supports universal pre-K, public school funding, tuition caps.

healthcare.summary: Proposes a mixed healthcare system guaranteeing basic care to all while keeping private insurance options, establishing at least one federally qualified health center in every county with low-cost or free services, and granting full-practice authority to certified nurse practitioners to encourage providers to work in rural areas.
healthcare.short: Proposes guaranteed basic care, county health centers, rural providers.

energy.summary: Says every person has the right to clean air, water, and land, and supports alternate energy resources such as solar, geothermal, or wind power to lower electricity costs; in a questionnaire she said data centers should not be allowed on farmland, public land, or land of historical or environmental value.
energy.short: Supports solar, geothermal, wind power; opposes data centers on farmland.

economy.summary: His campaign lists working to grow the economy and cutting government red tape among his priorities, citing support for small businesses, farmers and agribusiness, and increasing rural access to high-speed internet.
economy.short: Campaign cites growing economy, cutting red tape, rural broadband.

taxes.summary: Names elimination of school property taxes as a most pressing issue and supports a Taxpayer Protection Act constitutional amendment to prevent state spending from growing beyond revenue forecasts from the Pennsylvania Independent Fiscal Office.
taxes.short: Supports eliminating school property taxes; constitutional spending limit.

abortion.summary: His campaign site lists 'Defending the Unborn' among his priorities; the site does not detail specific abortion legislation or exceptions.
abortion.short: Campaign lists defending the unborn among his priorities.

energy.summary: As the incumbent, introduced legislation to let electric distribution companies invest in and own baseload power plants again, with net revenue from open-market electricity sales returned to consumers; he cites PJM forecasts of large baseload retirements and says immediate action is needed to keep power reliable and affordable.
energy.short: Proposes letting utilities own baseload plants, returning revenue to consumers.

guns.summary: His campaign site lists protecting Second Amendment rights among his priorities, and says he works to strengthen emergency services and support first responders.
guns.short: Campaign lists protecting Second Amendment rights, supporting first responders.
